Subject: Parity Validation: Lendwise model-fit hypothesis & next steps

Hi Sara / Tom — great call this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a proposed plan so we’re aligned before we kick off the eval sprint:

Summary of needs
- Primary use case: customer support triage + short-form answers from transactional docs (invoices, policy KB).
- Current in-house baseline: sequence-to-sequence model tuned on internal transcripts (proprietary), latency target <= 250ms p95, throughput 20 reqs/s, and strict hallucination tolerance.
- Key acceptance signals you mentioned: intent accuracy, hallucination rate, and answer faithfulness for invoice extraction.

Redwood hypothesis / recommended models to trial (initial list)
- Open candidates (fast trial path):
  * Llama 3 13B (q4_k_mixed) — good cost/latency profile for short responses
  * MPT-30B-instruct (int8) — stronger on instruction-following / extraction tasks but higher latency
- Proprietary baseline to compare: Lendwise seq2seq-v3 (your current tuned model)

Benchmarks & artifacts I’m attaching / linking
- Attached: lendwise_prompt_set_v1.json — prompt bundle + representative test cases from today
- Attached: parity_bench_results_template.xlsx — evaluation template we’ll use to collect metrics
- Drive: redwood_eval_readme.md (link above) — how we run the eval harness + metric definitions

Suggested acceptance thresholds (draft)
- Intent accuracy >= 95% vs baseline on the holdout set
- Hallucination rate <= 2% on sampled QA pairs (manual review protocol included)
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for open model variants on a Dedicated 1-GPU pilot (we can tighten target after baseline run)

Proposed next steps / timeline
1) We drop your prompt set into Redwood eval harness and run an automated parity sweep across the 2 open candidates + your baseline (ownership: Neha). Target: 8 business days.
2) Ben to size a Dedicated pilot (config + cost) and provide a short proposal by EOD Thu.
3) Sara / Tom to confirm any security review windows (you mentioned Thurs security sync).
4) If parity looks good, we’ll scope a 4-week pilot with dedicated routing and canari policy.

If this looks right, I’ll assign the eval ticket and calendar the kickoff.

Thanks — Vivek

- Hallucination definition: is Redwood using a token-level hallucination heuristic or human adjudication? We’ll need a small manual sample for compliance.
- Data sensitivity: a subset of the prompt set includes PII-like invoice numbers. We’ll need to confirm encryption-at-rest & access controls for the pilot.

Yes to Neha owning the eval run — can you also capture an initial smoke test (5k requests) so we can get a sense of latency on our traffic pattern? We have an internal security review on Thursday afternoon; if we can get a one-pager on data handling before then that would be ideal.

Vivek — I’ll pick this up. Notes for the eval plan and some additions to the acceptance criteria:

Eval harness basics
- I’ll run Redwood’s eval suite (scripted) against the attached prompt set. We’ll generate three result vectors: open model A (Llama 3 13B q4), open model B (MPT-30B-int8), and your local baseline export.
- Automated metrics: intent accuracy, exact-match on extraction fields, token-level probability flags (for hallucination scoring), latency distributions.
- Manual review: 200 sampled QA pairs split 4 ways for adjudication (we’ll provide a short guideline doc).

Additional acceptance items
- Stability: variance in p95 latency across runs <= 10%
- Regression guard: open model must not underperform baseline by >3% on extraction exact-match
- Cost estimate: report cost per 1k tokens and projected monthly bill for your expected 2M interactions

Security & data handling
- For the smoke test I will scrub invoice numbers in the prompt set unless you explicitly provide a redacted file. If you want exact numbers we’ll need a short SA agreement for limited ingest.

I’ve attached redwood_eval_readme.md with the exact commands and expected deliverables. I’ll create a shared results spreadsheet (using the template Vivek attached) and invite the Lendwise team once the first run completes — targeted completion: EOB next Monday (26 Apr).

-Neha

Subject: Fwd: Parity Validation: resource sizing & latency notes

Hi Sara / Tom — adding some initial sizing guidance and tradeoffs we discussed offline:

- Llama 3 13B (q4) on a single A10G-equivalent GPU: should meet near-target latency for short answers (p95 ~220-320ms depending on batching). Cost-effective for pilot and easy to scale horizontally.
- MPT-30B (int8) requires an A100/80GB or equivalent; stronger on instruction/extraction but p95 likely 350-550ms unless we shard / optimize kernels.
- Baseline export: if you want identical inference behavior we’ll need the baseline model artifact; otherwise we’ll run the exported weights you sent earlier and note any architecture mismatches in the report.

Pilot proposal (high level)
- 2-week smoke + parity run (Neha) — deliverables: results sheet, 200-sample manual review, latency/cost summary.
- 4-week dedicated pilot (if parity passes): we’ll provision a dedicated instance with autoscale to match your SLA windows and a canary policy for fallbacks.

Cost & Doc notes: I’ll drop a short PDF with cost bands into the Drive folder (link above) and post an estimated monthly bill based on your 2M interactions.

-Ben
